newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge up after Yeltsin's speech.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge up after Yeltsin's speech.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged up in early trade on Thursday following President Boris Yeltsin's address to parliament, traders said.
But the 23-share Russian Trading System index opened at 310.30, down from Wednesday's 311.10 close.

At 0815 GMT utility UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.2150 from $0.2085 at Wednesday's close, utility Irkutskenergo IRGZ.RTS edged up to $0.2600 from $0.2505, Gazprom GAZP.RTS rose to $0.6200 from $0.5985 and Rostelekom RTKM.RTS telecoms company was $3.88 after $3.85.
"The market is up about half a percent as a result of his speech," said Alfa-Capital trader Dmitry Lobanov, adding buying was mostly Russian.
However, traders said Yeltsin's speech, in which he promised to restore order to Russia, did not come up to market expectations.
"Everyone was waiting for an annoucement about appointments," Lobanov said.
Yeltsin said he would annouce a shake-up in his government in the coming days.
The cabinet will meet at 3 p.m. (1200 GMT) and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin is expected to announce new appointments then.
"He did not say anything sensational, there were only declarations," a trader said. "On the other hand people will be satisfied by his looks and after this the market may go up."
He said the effect of Yeltsin's speech would be delayed and prices would go up either later in the day or next weeks.
